edition: C. É. Ruelle, Damascii successoris Dubitationes et solutiones de primis principiis, in Platonis Parmenidem, Paris 1889, vol. 1

misprints.reason: an acute for the circumflex of the aorist infinitive, which the edition prints as διαστῆναι three times on p. 171
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 75, 21, read προόδους, the accusative plural of πρόοδος; the file already reads it
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 77, 23, read διεκρίθη, the aorist indicative; the page sets an iota subscript under the η, and the file already reads διεκρίθη
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 80, 4, read πρόοδον; the page sets the acute on the second ο, and the file already reads πρόοδον
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 99, 3 (note), read ἀπαντησόμεθα, the word of l. 3 that the note takes as its lemma (the list prints ἀπαντήσομεθα); the file already reads it
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 107, 1, read Χάους, the genitive of Χάος; the file already reads it
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 158, 6: "Ita interpunge: οὐ γάρ, ἐπειδὴ"; the page has no comma after γὰρ
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 163, 19, read ὑποτιθοῖτο: the circumflex of the optative on οῖ
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 176, 1, read ἑνιαίαν: a circumflex cannot stand before the long final syllable

Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 219, 10: "μαρτύρια. — (Not. inf.) μαρτυρίᾳ Kopp.": the page prints in the text the conjecture of Kopp, which belongs in the note, and ἐπαγαγεῖν takes μαρτύρια as its object

Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 219, 10: "μαρτύρια. — (Not. inf.) μαρτυρίᾳ Kopp.": the editor moves Kopp's conjecture, which the page prints in the text, to a lower note, which this copy does not print
Ruelle's Corrigenda (vol. 2 pp. 389-390), P. 225, 1, read ὕπαρξίς: the page has the acute the enclitic ἐστι adds to the last syllable, but not the acute of the word on its first

the page sets the acute on the ε. παραπτέσθαι is itself a Greek word, the aorist infinitive of παραπέτομαι, "fly past", but the sense of the passage (πόρρωθεν καὶ μόλις καὶ ἀμυδρότατά πη παραπτέσθαι ἢ παρυπονοεῖν) wants παράπτεσθαι, "touch lightly", the present infinitive of παράπτομαι, with the acute on the second α
the page sets the acute on the υ; ἁπλουστάτη, the feminine of the superlative, has it on the α before the long final η

misprints_note: Each entry is a word of the printed edition that the page misprints. The corpus text reads `corpus` in the passage `locus`; the page and line given print `print`. `reason` says why the printed form is a misprint. Where the page divides or joins words, or leaves out or adds a word, `print` and `corpus` have different numbers of words; an empty `print` means the page leaves out the words `corpus` gives, and an empty `corpus` means the corpus leaves out words the page prints.
what: Words the corpus corrects where the printed edition has an evident misprint
